summary: Planned tier2-webhook at scale feature: one milestone M1 holding five steps — M1-S01 object-model (Integration_Failure__c with twelve fields and two restricted picklists, Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c, the Tier2_Escalation__e platform event), M1-S02 access (OnCall_Tool_EC External Credential, OnCall_Tool SecuredEndpoint Named Credential, Tier2_Webhook_Admin permission set; human_gate true), M1-S03 automation (the Case escalation trigger, publish-and-enqueue service, webhook Queueable with Finalizer retry, the resend path and three test classes), M1-S04 automation (hourly Schedulable channel-health check), and M1-S05 docs (the build-level package.xml carrying the Apex members and the compiled deploy order). Fourteen decisions recorded, eleven citing a decision-tree branch verbatim and four resolved from a skill reference with adr_required true. Twelve assumptions, each naming the step it constrains. No blocked steps. build_plan.py validate exits 0 with zero warnings.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per the build-planner rubric: four decisions (D3, D10, D13, D14) were resolved from a source_reference rather than a tree branch and carry adr_required true, and one informational clarification (Q43) reached the plan open with no default and became assumption A1. Every agent, skill, template, tree branch and declared checker resolves on disk; every checker was run on a throwaway fixture; validate exits 0 with no warnings; no step is blocked.

fit_gap.requirement: Notify the on-call tool within a minute of a Tier 2 escalation, with retry and a visible failure record
Publish an escalation event the existing external ops dashboard can consume
A visible failure record an admin can see, triage and re-send from
The on-call tool's API key must never be stored in code or in a custom setting
Alert a named owner when the notification channel itself goes dark
The build deploys as one reviewable unit: a manifest and a written deploy order

decisions.decision: Fire-and-forget Queueable with Database.AllowsCallouts, Direction 1 only
Named Credential + External Credential (Custom); API key injected as X-API-Key by the credential
NamedPrincipal on a SecuredEndpoint credential, not PerUserPrincipal and not Legacy
JSON REST through templates/apex/HttpClient.cls, never a hand-built HttpRequest
Retry 429/502/503/504 and timeouts three times from the Finalizer with a MinimumQueueableDelayInMinutes backoff; 400/401/403/404/422 never retried
Idempotency-Key header of Case Id plus enqueue-time escalation timestamp, stored on the failure row
A Queueable Finalizer, attached first in execute(), guarantees the failure record on every terminal state
Apex trigger + handler + service, not a record-triggered Flow
Tier2_Escalation__e consumed by the dashboard over the Pub/Sub API
publishBehavior PublishAfterCommit, published from the escalating transaction's service layer rather than inside the Queueable
Hourly channel-health check is Schedulable Apex delegating to a Queueable, not a schedule-triggered Flow
Integration_Failure__c OWD Private plus object-scoped View All / Modify All on one narrow admin permission set
Cross-transaction suppression by the Tier2_Notified_At__c stamp and a ten-minute window, not AsyncOptions.DuplicateSignature
Tier2_Webhook_Admin is assigned to every user who can escalate a Case, because the Queueable calls out as the async context user rather than Automated Process
